title: Ray Dalio Warns of US Debt Crisis Within Three Years
summary: Bridgewater Associates Founder Ray Dalio warns that the US is approaching the limits of its debt cycle, predicting a potential crisis within three years as spending outpaces revenue. He cautions that rising borrowing costs and weakening demand from key foreign buyers may squeeze lower-income borrowers first. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Barclays’ Lauren Lieberman on PepsiCo Earnings
summary: Barclays US Equity Research Analyst Lauren Lieberman said PepsiCo’s positive share-price reaction was less a sign of broad optimism than a rebound after a period of weakness. She viewed the company’s acknowledgment that the status quo is not working—and that changes are needed—as the day’s biggest surprise, while its lowered full-year expectations were widely anticipated. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: True Religion CEO on Company Transformation and Gen Z Customers
summary: True Religion CEO Michael Buckley discusses the brands comeback, noting its origins as a premium women’s denim brand in the early 2000s and its recent pivot toward more affordable offerings. Gen Z interest and attention from celebrities have helped revive the brand. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Patagonia CEO: Insist on Growing at Own Pace
summary: Patagonia CEO Ryan Gellert, discusses the company’s approach to environmental activism, Gellert’s views on growth and profitability, and where he believes leaders across the industry stand. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Arc’teryx CEO on Product Expansion & Consumer Demand
summary: Stuart Haselden CEO of Arc'teryx discusses the company's aims to nearly double revenue over the next five years by building on two strategic priorities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fixed Income Leaders Dialogue
summary: The fixed income landscape is evolving as public and private credit converge, AI-related financing accelerates and investors navigate a more complex credit cycle. TCW CIO of Fixed Income Bryan Whalen and Blackstone Credit & Insurance’s Philip Sherrill were in conversation with Bloomberg’s Scarlet Fu at the Bloomberg Future of Fixed Income 2026 conference in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chipotle Jumps on Report Starbucks Has Explored Takeover
summary:
Shares of Chipotle Mexican Grill jumped after the Financial Times reported that Starbucks Corp. has worked with advisers in recent months on a takeover proposal for the burrito chain.

The status of the takeover plans couldn’t be immediately learned and a mega deal of this size might never get off the ground, the FT said, citing people familiar with the matter. Brian Niccol, Starbucks’ chief executive officer since 2024, previously spent six years as the top executive at Chipotle, where he spearheaded a period of rapid growth. 

For more, we speak with Redd Brown, Bloomberg News Consumer Reporter. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Bond ETFs Are Reshaping Portfolio Construction
summary: Bond ETFs are moving into their next phase, with active strategies, new product structures and more specialized exposures changing how investors build fixed income portfolios. State Street Investment Management’s Ethan Balakier, BondBloxx’s Joanna Gallegos and Schwab Asset Management’s Riz Hussain joined Bloomberg Intelligence’s Eric Balchunas at the Bloomberg Future of Fixed Income 2026 conference in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Rises After Trump Says US Won’t Attack Iran Before Midterms
summary: Gold rose from a two-month low, with traders assessing the outlook for energy prices after President Donald Trump said the US won’t attack Iran before the midterm elections.
